rules.rule: Check for emergency patient airway, breathing and circulation signs
rules.problem: Type and structure right: one check_for covering the response/pulse/breathing flow, the four ABC-D columns and both footnote-3 definitions. The page has no presenting complaint, so an or-trigger on any recorded emergency sign is a reasonable anchor. Minor: Acute confusion (c033) is a redundant child of Clouded consciousness; Cardiac arrest (c002) is inferred rather than on the page. Not modelled (management branches, not triage): 'If unconscious' (oropharyngeal airway), 'neck injury suspected', 'vomiting' (recovery position), 'known heart problem or severe infection suspected' (fluid choice).

probable is right ('tension pneumothorax likely'). The and/or structure is a literal reading of 'If sudden breathlessness, more resonant/decreased breath sounds/pain on 1 side, deviated trachea': commas as and, slashes as or. That makes deviated trachea (a late sign) mandatory, so the rule will miss most tension pneumothoraces that a nurse would call from sudden breathlessness plus one-sided signs. The page's punctuation is genuinely ambiguous; a clinician should confirm whether the comma list is all-of or any-of (e.g. sudden breathlessness and any of the rest).

probable is right (footnote 3 'shock likely'). Requiring all five of SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, RR > 30, confusion/restlessness and weakness is the literal comma-as-and reading; the main text's 'If shock³/SBP < 80' treats SBP < 80 as the core of shock, so a patient with SBP 70, pulse 120 and RR 28 would not be labelled shock here. Triage is unaffected (SBP < 80 and pulse ≥ 100 each give Emergency on their own), so only the diagnosis label is at stake. Clinician to confirm the intended logic. Acute confusion (c052) is redundant.

rules.rule: Emergency: emergency patient unresponsive, pulseless or not breathing
rules.problem: Emergency is justified: this is the emergency-patient page and these are the CPR / rescue-breathing branches. Cardiac arrest (c058) is inferred from 'Start CPR' rather than named; harmless.

rules.rule: Emergency: emergency patient with airway, breathing, circulation or consciousness compromise
rules.problem: Emergency is justified by the red box 'Give urgent attention to the emergency patient' and 'Manage further and refer urgently'. The or-list mirrors each 'If ...' management trigger on the page; the bradycardia block correctly nests 'pulse < 50 and unstable (...)' with footnote 3 inlined; BP < 90/60 split as SBP < 90 or DBP < 60 follows the gold page. Note pulse ≥ 100 alone reaches Emergency, which is what the page's fluid criterion says.

summary: No invented or misplaced content: all 90 claims trace to page 16 text in the right rule and role, all 44 SNOMED concepts exist, numbers and comparison directions match, and Emergency is justified by the page heading. The most consequential question is interpretive: both 'likely' rules read the page's comma lists as all-of, so tension pneumothorax requires a deviated trachea and shock requires all five footnote features, which is literal but probably stricter than intended; triage priority is unaffected because each vital threshold fires Emergency on its own. Minor: Acute confusion is a redundant narrower child of Clouded consciousness (c033, c052), and Cardiac arrest (c002, c058) is inferred from 'no pulse → start CPR' rather than named on the page.
